analysis.investment_thesis: KSB is a genuinely high-quality industrial compounder — zero debt, 24.5% ROCE, 14-16% earnings CAGR over nine years — but at 44x EV/EBITDA and 58x P/E, the stock prices in a decade of perfection with zero margin of safety. Second-level thinking demands we ask not "is this a good business?" but "what does INR 16,850 Cr already assume?" — and the answer is: flawless execution, no cycle risk, and perpetual 15%+ growth.
key_strengths: Zero debt (D/E = 0.00), pristine balance sheet with INR 167 Cr cash and steadily growing reserves to INR 1,644 Cr
Exceptional capital efficiency: ROCE of 24.5% sustained over multiple cycles, with net profit CAGR of 16.4% over 9 years
German parent (KSB SE) technology moat, 69.8% promoter holding, and diversified end-markets (water, energy, oil & gas, chemicals) providing demand resilience
key_risks: Valuation admits no error: at 44x EV/EBITDA on INR 447 Cr EBITDA, a compression to 25x (still generous for an industrial) implies ~44% downside before any earnings deterioration
FY2025 FCF collapsed to essentially zero (OCF INR 93 Cr minus capex INR 94 Cr) — FCF yield on INR 16,850 Cr market cap is ~0.5%, catastrophically below any reasonable hurdle rate
Erratic FCF conversion across 5 years (122, 25, -67, 49, 88, 0) raises questions about working capital discipline; CWIP nearly tripled (INR 32 Cr → INR 89 Cr) as capex cycle intensifies
red_flags: FCF yield ~0% in FY2025 — paying INR 16,850 Cr for a business generating no free cash is speculation, not investment
EV/EBITDA of 44x for a 14% grower implies a PEG of ~3x — consensus is uniformly bullish on India capex theme, a classic late-cycle sentiment signal
Revenue growth actually decelerating at the margin: FY2024 revenue growth ~12.7%, FY2025 ~6.4% — but multiple hasn't compressed
analysis.detailed_analysis:
KSB is the textbook case of a great business at a terrible price. The fundamentals are admirable: nine years of 14-16% compounding, virtually debt-free balance sheet, 24.5% ROCE, and the durable advantage of being a technology licensee of a global pumps-and-valves leader serving critical infrastructure. The aftermarket spares and services business provides recurring revenue that smooths cyclical swings. This is exactly the kind of business I respect — but respecting a business and paying any price for it are entirely different things.

At INR 968, the market is pricing KSB as if the India capex supercycle continues uninterrupted, margins expand, and FCF converts cleanly from earnings for the next 10+ years. The earnings yield is a meager 1.7%, and FY2025 FCF yield is effectively 0%. If EBITDA multiples revert to a still-generous 25x — a level appropriate for quality industrials globally — the stock loses roughly 44% before touching earnings risk. The greed/fear pendulum in Indian industrials has swung sharply toward greed since 2021; this name is a beneficiary of that euphoria, not a beneficiary of intrinsic value discovery. Downside scenario: a slowdown in government infrastructure spend or a general de-rating of Indian industrials could see this trade at 25-30x EV/EBITDA — implying INR 500-600 range. There is no margin of safety here.
